examples.note: Tórshavn — fixed network ranges begin with 3

notes: The Faroe Islands are a self-governing part of Denmark but have their own country code +298, separate from Denmark's +45.
All numbers are 6 digits with no trunk prefix or area codes, written as three pairs.
The islands received a code beginning with 2 (a range normally allocated to Africa) because the European 3xx and 4xx ranges were exhausted.

examples.note: Nuuk — 31/32 serve the capital in Sermersooq

notes: Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark but has its own country code +299.
All numbers are 6 digits, written as three pairs, with no trunk prefix.
The first two digits still carry rough geographic meaning for fixed lines.

formats.international: +39 06 698 XXXXX — the assigned code +379 is not in general use

patterns.label: Vatican offices via the Italian plan

examples.note: Vatican office — reached through Rome's 06 area code, block 698

notes: +379 is assigned to Vatican City by the ITU but is effectively unused for public dialling. Almost every reachable Vatican number sits inside the Italian numbering plan as +39 06 698xxxxx.
The 698 block within Rome's 06 area code is reserved for the Holy See.
Because these are Italian numbers, Italy's rule applies: the leading 0 of 06 is part of the number and is kept when dialling from abroad (+39 06 698…, not +39 6 698…).
Numbers on +379 exist only as short internal exchange extensions and are not publicly routable.
sources: ITU-T E.164 assigned country codes: https://www.itu.int/pub/T-SP-E.164D
